title: The Hook: The Mirror Mystery
text: Have you ever looked in the mirror and noticed your nose looks exactly like your father's? Or perhaps you sneeze exactly the way your grandfather does! It's a real-world mystery happening right inside your home. Why do we look and act so much like our family members?

title: Socratic Thinking: The Hidden Instruction
text: Imagine a tiny mango seed planted in the soil. How does the seed 'know' it must grow into a mango tree and not a neem tree? Where does this hidden instruction come from? What do you think?

content.title: Discovery: The Blueprint of Life
content.description: Just like a builder uses a blueprint to build a house, our bodies have a hidden blueprint passed down from our parents. This diagram represents how traits from a mother and father combine in a child.

title: The Reveal: Heredity
text: This passing of traits from parents to children is called **Heredity**. The word comes from the Latin root 'hereditatem' meaning inheritance. Your body is built using instructions combined from both your mother and your father!

content.preview_text: Features or characteristics that are passed down from parents to their children, such as eye color, hair type, or even the shape of the earlobes.

content.question: Which of the following is an example of an inherited trait?
options: Knowing how to ride a bicycle
Having brown eyes like your mother
Having a scar from a playground fall

content.title: Reflection: The Family Mirror
content.text: Look closely at your family members today. Do you have your mother's hair? Your father's height? Write down three features you share with your relatives. Ask your parents who they look like!

title: Connection: The Web of Life
text: It's not just humans! A puppy inherits its fur color from its dog parents. A rose plant inherits its petal color from the parent plant. All living things pass on their traits. This connects humans to the broader animal and plant kingdom.

content.title: Mastery: The Family Tree Detective
content.text: Draw a family tree going back to your grandparents. Track one specific trait (like curly hair, a dimple, or eye color) and map how it traveled through the generations to you!

content.title: Nature vs. Nurture
content.text: Remember, not everything is inherited. Things we learn (like playing the guitar) or things that happen to us (like getting a scar) are called 'Acquired Traits'. They are not passed to the next generation.

content.title: The Polio Misconception
content.text: A common mistake is thinking that all diseases are inherited. For example, Polio is caused by a virus and affects the legs. If a parent has polio, their child will NOT inherit it. It is an acquired disease, not an inherited genetic trait.

content.question: If a person gets a scar on their arm from an accident, will their future children be born with the same scar?
options: Yes, because it becomes part of their body.
No, because a scar is an acquired trait, not inherited.
Only if both parents have a scar.
Yes, physical traits are always passed down.
